task.title: Variable and color fonts
task.shortdesc: A variable font changes its design along axes, such as weight, width and optical size. A color font draws its glyphs with the colors of a palette. The font file must provide the axis or the palette that you request.

context.p: Each axis of a variable font has a four-letter tag. The registered tags are wght for the weight, wdth for the width, slnt and ital for the slant, and opsz for the optical size. A font can also have axes with other tags. The font can have named instances, which are ready-made combinations of axis values, such as "Condensed Bold".

For the standard axes, use the properties that you use with any font: font-weight controls wght, font-width controls wdth, and font-style controls slnt and ital. They also take part in the choice of the face. Declare the range that the font covers in an @font-face rule, as Font resources and descriptors explains.

info.p: A font with an optical size axis changes the details of its glyphs with the size of the text, for example thinner strokes at large sizes. Use font-optical-sizing to turn it on or off. With auto, which is the initial value, CSSMedia sets the opsz axis from the font size, within the range of the axis. With none, it leaves the axis at the value that you set or at its default:
Use font-variation-settings to set the axes by their tags. The value is normal, or a comma-separated list of an axis tag in quotes followed by a number. The number can be a fraction or negative:

CSSMedia clamps a number to the range of the axis. It ignores an axis that the font does not have, and if a tag occurs more than once, the last value wins. This property does not take part in the choice of the face. The font-variation-settings descriptor of @font-face sets the same values as the defaults of a face. The values of the property come last, so they win.
A color font has one or more palettes, which are numbered lists of colors, starting at 0. Use font-palette to choose one:

ul.li: normal: the usual palette of the font, which is palette 0 in most fonts.
light and dark: the first palette that the font marks for light or for dark backgrounds. If the font has none, CSSMedia uses normal.
A name that starts with two hyphens, such as --night: a palette that you define with @font-palette-values. If no rule defines it, CSSMedia uses normal.
palette-mix(): a palette that mixes the colors of other palettes.

info.p: palette-mix() takes a color interpolation method and two or more palettes, each with an optional percentage. The method is the one that color-mix() uses, such as in oklab. The palettes are any value of font-palette, including another palette-mix(). Palettes without a percentage share the remainder equally. If the percentages add up to more than 100%, CSSMedia scales them to 100%, and if they add up to less, the colors become more transparent by the missing share. Use the @font-palette-values rule to give a name to a palette. The name starts with two hyphens. Three descriptors define the palette:

ul.li: font-family lists the families that the palette is for. It is required. Generic families are not allowed.
base-palette is the palette that you start from: light, dark or a palette number. If you omit it, or the font has no such palette, it is palette 0.

override-colors replaces colors of the base palette. The value is a comma-separated list of pairs of a palette number and a color. An index that the palette does not have is ignored, and if an index occurs more than once, the last color wins.

info.p: The colors of override-colors must be absolute: named colors, hexadecimal colors and numeric functions such as rgb() in any color space. A color that depends on the context, such as currentColor, makes the descriptor invalid. If two rules have the same name, the last one wins.
